title: Terminating intuitionistic propositional proof search

based_on.title: Contraction-free sequent calculi for intuitionistic logic: a correction
Constructive Logic (15-317), Lecture 11: G4ip, a contraction-free calculus
based_on.pages: pp.1–9: rules, soundness and numerical weight; corrected completeness taken from Dyckhoff 2018

summary: Enumerate all backward G4ip alternatives, reconstruct actual certificates, and decide finite native intuitionistic consequence with a proved sufficient fuel bound.
abstract: Trying the first branch of a proof search can fail even when another branch closes immediately. We turn the decreasing G4ip rules into an exhaustive procedure that keeps its alternatives in a finite list, solves every premise of a selected rule, and backtracks when a choice fails. A successful run returns the actual primitive proof tree. The endsequent’s weight supplies enough fuel to find every existing proof, so a full failure proves nonderivability. Expanding native negation connects this computation to the original intuitionistic language, and explicit examples distinguish backtracking from premature fuel exhaustion.
